api-server.title: API Server
api-server.description: Node.js/Express REST API. Handles authentication (JWT/bcrypt), CRUD on notes, file uploads to MinIO. Bridges the frontend and backend networks. Single most security-critical component — compromise equals full data access.
api-server.justification_cia_rating: The API processes all user data. It bridges both Docker networks — a compromised API container can pivot into the internal data tier.

communication_links.title: PostgreSQL Connection
communication_links.description: Application-level SQL queries for user auth, notes CRUD. Uses parameterized queries (pg library) to prevent SQL injection. No TLS on the connection — traffic is plaintext within backend-net.

communication_links.title: Redis Session Store
communication_links.description: Session token storage and JWT revocation list. Password-protected (requirepass) but no TLS.

communication_links.title: MinIO File Storage
communication_links.description: INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: S3 API calls to MinIO over plain HTTP. Default minioadmin/minioadmin credentials are hardcoded in compose. Any container on backend-net can read all stored files.

aws-api-gateway.title: AWS API Gateway
aws-api-gateway.description: AWS API Gateway (HTTP API) fronting the ECS API containers in production. Routes traffic from the ALB to backend ECS tasks. INTENTIONAL: No usage plan or throttling policy configured. No WAF association on the API gateway stage. Auth relies entirely on the API server (JWT) — no gateway-level auth enforcement.

technologies.name: cloud-api-gateway
technologies.description: A managed cloud API gateway (AWS API Gateway, Azure APIM, GCP Cloud Endpoints)

aws-api-gateway.justification_cia_rating: API gateway is the single internet entry point in production. No rate limiting = credential stuffing and cost amplification risk. WAF absence leaves XSS/SQLi traffic unfiltered before it reaches the API.

communication_links.title: Route to ECS API
communication_links.description: HTTP forward from API Gateway to the ECS-hosted API containers via ALB. Traffic is within the AWS VPC — no public routing for backend traffic.

aws-ses.title: AWS SES
aws-ses.description: AWS Simple Email Service used for transactional email delivery (note-share invitations, account verification). Managed service — not custom-developed. SES sending identity (domain) is verified; DKIM and SPF records are configured. No dedicated sending quota alarm; a compromised Lambda could exhaust the daily send limit and cause notification delivery failure.
aws-ses.justification_cia_rating: SES handles PII (email addresses). Sending quota exhaustion prevents delivery of account verification emails, blocking user registration. Email spoofing via insufficient SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment is possible if domain records are misconfigured.

browser-spa.title: Browser SPA
browser-spa.description: React Single Page Application served from Nginx. Users authenticate, manage notes, and upload files through this interface.
browser-spa.justification_cia_rating: Client-side code is public; the trust boundary here is user data entered into the browser. XSS would allow an attacker to exfiltrate session tokens.

communication_links.title: HTTPS to Nginx
communication_links.description: User-initiated HTTPS requests carrying credentials (login) and note content (create/edit). This is the only encrypted link in the chain.

build-pipeline.title: GitHub Actions Build Pipeline
build-pipeline.description: GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline. Builds Docker images, runs tests, pushes to ECR. INTENTIONAL: No SBOM generation (no Syft or CycloneDX step configured). No build provenance attestation (no SLSA provenance step). Hardcoded AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in workflow environment variables.
build-pipeline.justification_cia_rating: Build pipeline is a privileged component — it has read access to secrets and write access to the container registry. Compromise = full supply chain injection. No SBOM means post-build vulnerability tracking is impossible.

communication_links.title: Push Image to Registry
communication_links.description: docker push to AWS ECR after build completes. Images are tagged with the git commit SHA and pushed without cryptographic signing (no Cosign step).

container-registry.title: AWS ECR Container Registry
container-registry.description: AWS Elastic Container Registry storing VaultNote Docker images (api, nginx). INTENTIONAL: Image vulnerability scanning is disabled (ECR Basic scanning only, not Enhanced/Inspector). Images are not signed — no Cosign/Sigstore policy enforced. Repository is private but no admission controller validates signatures at deploy time.

technologies.name: container-registry
technologies.description: A cloud container image registry (AWS ECR, GCP GCR, Azure ACR)

container-registry.justification_cia_rating: Container registry is the final source of truth for deployed images. Tampering with registry contents (image swap or layer injection) propagates malicious code to every deployment. No signing verification means a registry compromise is undetectable until damage is done.

ecs-platform.title: ECS Container Platform
ecs-platform.description: AWS ECS (Fargate) running the API and Nginx containers in production. INTENTIONAL: ECR Enhanced Scanning (Inspector v2) is not enabled. Running containers are not scanned post-deployment for newly disclosed CVEs. Container images are pulled from ECR without signature verification.

technologies.name: container-platform
technologies.description: A platform for hosting and executing containers

ecs-platform.justification_cia_rating: ECS runs the production API containers. Container escape or image tampering grants access to the application runtime and its mounted secrets. No image scanning means known CVEs in base images are undetected until exploitation.

communication_links.title: Pull Images from ECR
communication_links.description: ECS task pulls Docker images from ECR at task launch. Images are not verified against signatures before execution.

lambda-notifier.title: Lambda Email Notifier
lambda-notifier.description: AWS Lambda function that sends transactional emails (note-share invitations, account verification) triggered by SQS messages from the API server. Processes user email addresses (PII) and note titles in notification payloads. INTENTIONAL: No dead letter queue (DLQ) configured on the SQS event source. Failed notifications are silently dropped after 3 retries with no audit trail.

technologies.name: serverless-function
technologies.description: A serverless compute function (AWS Lambda, GCP Cloud Functions, Azure Functions)

lambda-notifier.justification_cia_rating: Lambda processes email addresses and note titles. PII loss due to silent failure creates compliance issues (incomplete processing records). Overpermissive IAM role could be exploited to access other AWS resources.

communication_links.title: SES Email Send
communication_links.description: Lambda calls AWS SES to deliver transactional emails. IAM role grants ses:SendEmail only; no SendRawEmail permission. No SES sending rate limit configured on the IAM policy — a compromised Lambda could exhaust the SES daily quota.

llm-summarizer.title: LLM Note Summarizer
llm-summarizer.description: OpenAI-compatible LLM inference endpoint used to generate AI summaries of user notes on demand. Deployed as a containerised model proxy (LiteLLM) with a public API endpoint for testing. INTENTIONAL: Endpoint is internet-accessible and lacks authentication — the has-authentication tag is intentionally absent to demonstrate the finding. No adversarial input shield (Llama Guard or guardrails) is configured. System prompt contains internal business context visible to adversarial probing.

technologies.name: llm-inference-endpoint
technologies.description: An LLM inference endpoint — exposes a language model via API for text generation
aliases: llm-endpoint, llm-api, openai-compatible, inference-server, vllm, ollama, triton

llm-summarizer.justification_cia_rating: LLM endpoint processes user note content. Unauthenticated internet exposure allows arbitrary prompt submission, system prompt extraction via jailbreaks, and inference cost abuse. No guardrails means malicious inputs could generate harmful content or exfiltrate context window data.

communication_links.title: Query Vector Store
communication_links.description: LLM retrieves relevant note chunks from the vector store to build RAG context. Similarity search over user-owned embeddings.

communication_links.title: Call RAG Pipeline
communication_links.description: LLM inference endpoint triggers the RAG pipeline to build context from stored note embeddings before generating a summary response.

minio-storage.title: MinIO Object Storage
minio-storage.description: S3-compatible object store for file attachments. INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: Uses default minioadmin/minioadmin credentials (visible in docker-compose.yml) and stores files without encryption at rest. HTTP-only (no TLS) within the Docker network.

technologies.name: object-storage
technologies.description: Cloud object/blob storage (AWS S3, GCP GCS, Azure Blob Storage)

minio-storage.justification_cia_rating: Stores user file uploads which may contain sensitive documents. Default credentials + no encryption = trivial exfiltration by any process on backend-net.

nginx-proxy.title: Nginx Reverse Proxy
nginx-proxy.description: Nginx terminates TLS and forwards all API traffic to the Express server over plain HTTP (port 3000). This is the DMZ entry point.

technologies.name: reverse-proxy
technologies.description: A proxy hiding internal infrastructure from caller making requests. Can also reduce load

nginx-proxy.justification_cia_rating: Nginx is the single external entry point. Its compromise exposes all downstream services. Availability is critical — outage = full service outage.

communication_links.title: HTTP to API Server
communication_links.description: INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: Traffic between Nginx and the API server uses plaintext HTTP. An attacker with access to the Docker network (container escape, compromised sidecar) can intercept credentials, session tokens, and note content in transit.

postgresql-db.title: PostgreSQL Database
postgresql-db.description: Primary relational datastore. Contains users table (email + bcrypt password hash), notes table (title + content), and attachments metadata. INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: No encryption at rest (encryption: none).
postgresql-db.justification_cia_rating: Holds all user PII (email, hashed passwords) and all note content. Strictly confidential — unencrypted disk access exposes all data.

rag-pipeline.title: Note RAG Pipeline
rag-pipeline.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline that assembles context chunks from the vector store before forwarding to the LLM. Built on LangChain. INTENTIONAL: No input validation or injection guard on retrieved chunks (has-input-validation absent). A note containing prompt injection payloads could be retrieved as context and alter LLM behavior. No retrieval filtering — all results from the vector store are injected into context without relevance threshold or content sanitisation.

technologies.name: rag-pipeline
technologies.description: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline that retrieves documents and feeds them to an LLM

rag-pipeline.justification_cia_rating: RAG pipeline is the injection point between user-controlled note content and the LLM context window. Without input validation, a malicious note can manipulate the LLM into ignoring instructions, leaking system prompts, or generating harmful content on behalf of an attacker.

communication_links.title: Retrieve from Vector Store
communication_links.description: RAG pipeline queries the vector store for nearest-neighbor embeddings to build context chunks. Returns raw embedding text — no content filtering before injection into LLM context.

rds-postgresql.title: AWS RDS PostgreSQL
rds-postgresql.description: AWS RDS PostgreSQL instance (production). Replaces the Docker-based PostgreSQL in production deployments. Automated backups enabled (7-day retention). INTENTIONAL: Encryption at rest is disabled (storage_encrypted = false in Terraform). Public accessibility is off but subnet group is in app subnet (not data subnet), creating potential exposure via compromised app instances.

technologies.name: managed-database
technologies.description: A fully managed cloud database service (AWS RDS, Aurora, GCP Cloud SQL, Azure CosmosDB)

rds-postgresql.justification_cia_rating: Production database stores all user PII and note content. Encryption disabled means RDS snapshot exfiltration exposes all data in plaintext. Snapshot sharing misconfiguration (a common AWS incident) bypasses all access controls.

redis-cache.title: Redis Cache
redis-cache.description: In-memory store used as session store and JWT revocation list. INTENTIONAL MISCONFIGURATION: No encryption at rest. If Redis persistence is enabled and the RDB file is exfiltrated, session tokens are exposed.
redis-cache.justification_cia_rating: Session token exposure enables account takeover. Non-persistent by default but the container volume could persist RDB snapshots.

s3-notes-bucket.title: AWS S3 Notes Bucket
s3-notes-bucket.description: AWS S3 bucket storing file attachments for production deployments. Replaces MinIO S3-compatible storage in the cloud environment. Bucket is private (Block Public Access enabled) but server-side encryption is not configured. INTENTIONAL: SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS not enabled. Objects are stored unencrypted at the storage layer — provider-side access exposes raw data.

technologies.name: object-storage
technologies.description: Cloud object/blob storage (AWS S3, GCP GCS, Azure Blob Storage)

s3-notes-bucket.justification_cia_rating: S3 stores user-uploaded files which may contain sensitive documents. No SSE means provider-side access (support channel, storage engineer) reads raw data. third-party-shared because S3 is operated by AWS and subject to subprocessor data protection requirements. No DPA review completed.

source-repo.title: VaultNote Source Repository
source-repo.description: GitHub repository hosting the VaultNote monorepo (API, frontend, Terraform). Contains application secrets in compose files (minioadmin credentials visible in git history) and Terraform state references. INTENTIONAL: No branch protection rules configured — developers push directly to main, bypassing review and signed-commit requirements.
source-repo.justification_cia_rating: Source code is the root of the supply chain. Integrity is critical — malicious code injected here propagates to every built artifact. May contain leaked secrets.

communication_links.title: Push to Pipeline
communication_links.description: Git push triggers GitHub Actions workflow. The webhook carries the commit SHA and branch reference to the CI runner.

vector-store.title: VaultNote Vector Store
vector-store.description: Qdrant vector database storing embedding vectors for semantic search and RAG context retrieval. Vectors are generated by the embedding service from user note content. INTENTIONAL: No encryption at rest configured (encryption: none). The vector store is queryable by the LLM pipeline and the API server without row-level isolation — all user embeddings share the same collection. No access control list separates per-user embedding queries.

technologies.name: vector-store
technologies.description: A vector database storing embedding vectors (used in RAG pipelines)
aliases: vector-database, embedding-store, pinecone, weaviate, qdrant, chroma, milvus

vector-store.justification_cia_rating: Embedding vectors encode semantic information from user notes. Even without raw text, vectors can be used to infer content via inversion attacks. Unencrypted storage and lack of per-user access control create cross-tenant leakage risk.
